content.text:
**v0.36.6 is released** with the new batching wording: https://github.com/cv/pit/releases/tag/v0.36.6

**The change** is in `src/tool/metadata.ts`. The old `Promise.all` guideline is replaced with:

> "Plan each step before calling: one program should gather every read, search, and probe the step needs (Promise.all, or workspace.batch for files; Promise.allSettled for optional probes), and one should make all its edits to different files. Each tool call is a round trip that resends the context. Sequence only dependent work and edits to the same file."

Pit sends this guideline both to Pi and to pi-durable hosts such as pi-action.

**Size limit:** the new line is longer than the old one, so the tool's fixed prompt text went from about 5,990 to 6,176 characters. That broke the size limit in `test/tool/prompt.test.ts`, so I raised it from 6,000 to 6,200, with a comment pointing to #375. I didn't add a test that checks the wording itself.

**How it shipped:**
- PR #377, with a commit for the change and a commit for the release (version bump, `CHANGELOG.md` entry, README pinned install). It was rebase-merged after all 5 checks passed.
- Check, tests, coverage and package check passed locally, and CI passed on the merged `main` commit `8e098d5`.
- The tag `v0.36.6` is on that commit, and the Release workflow succeeded.
- `release.verifyPublished` confirmed the release points at the tagged commit and has no assets. A fresh clone of the tag installed and ran the sandbox (version 0.36.6).

I didn't run the hands-on Pi smoke test from the release guide; this release only changes prompt text. I also left this issue open, because the real test is whether sessions take fewer turns. `sessions.analyzeRecent` can compare tool calls per task before and after the update; close the issue when you're satisfied.
